task1_safe_surface.question: how many pub safe fns can reach an unsafe operation, which are reachable from safe Rust outside the crate, and how many closure obligations are reachable only through unsafe exports

method.fn_detection: regex \bfn NAME over stripped source; qualifier/visibility walk backwards; body brace-match
method.call_graph: name-based: identifiers followed by '(' plus .method( plus macro!(; resolves a name to every definition with that name (over-approximation); Self::/Type:: resolve via the last segment
method.reachability: transitive fixed point: safe fn reaches unsafe iff its own body has an `unsafe` token or an unsafe fn, or a callee does
method.external: vis == pub, every enclosing inline mod pub, and for methods either the type name has a pub definition or the impl is reachable through the type; excludes #[doc(hidden)], #[cfg(test)], and `tests` mods
limitations: not a rustc-level resolution: trait-object dispatch, generics, closures and macro-expanded call edges are not resolved; the graph over-approximates call edges by name and under-approximates dynamic dispatch

re-exports (`pub use private_mod::x`) are not followed; a pub fn in a private module re-exported is counted as external only if its own module chain is pub, so the external count is a lower bound for that shape
fn-level attributes on the same line as the signature are captured; attributes are matched by balanced brackets on stripped text

sensitivity.stricter_external_rule: vis == pub, every enclosing inline mod pub, and for an impl method the type must be defined pub in the same file; excludes #[doc(hidden)]/#[cfg(test)]/tests
sensitivity.note: the difference (28) is impl methods whose type is not pub in the same file; the order of magnitude and every conclusion are unchanged

task1_safe_surface.quic_stub_note: 33 of the 46 safe pub extern C raw-pointer functions are the QUIC/stream stubs in ssl_lib.rs; each body is `let _ = (args); <constant>` and the pointer is never used.

obligations_reachable_from_external_safe.caveat: the lexical graph resolves calls by name and does not follow function-pointer tables or macro-expanded edges, so the reached count is a lower bound (the unsafe-entry-only count is an upper bound). The 21 reviewed obligations were adjudicated by direct caller reads instead.

task1_safe_surface.conclusion: The criterion-3 scope is the safe-pub surface, not the 290 obligations as a whole: 879 safe pub fn definitions (122 plain Rust ABI, 757 extern C) are reachable from safe Rust, and 477 of them reach an unsafe operation. The b78 argument's premise that 'the mechanism entry points are pub unsafe extern C, so a safe-Rust caller cannot invoke one without an unsafe block' is false for the 757 safe extern C exports, at least 6 of which dereference caller pointers. The recorded 'crate-wide safe pub fn count is 202' could not be reproduced: 202 is neither 879 nor the 122 plain-Rust-ABI count, and no tool is recorded for it (evidence defect).

dynamic_data_ctx_free_func.contract_quote: `CRYPTO_EX_free`'s ex_data contract: `ptr` is NULL or the value currently stored at the index this hook was registered for ... and that value is a live `DynamicDataCtx` which the enclosing ENGINE owns through its own ex_data slot.
dynamic_data_ctx_free_func.callers_from_safe_code: none. The name occurs only at its definition (eng_dyn.rs:415) and in the `Some(dynamic_data_ctx_free_func)` argument of CRYPTO_get_ex_new_index (eng_dyn.rs:499-504), inside `dynamic_get_data_ctx` (private `unsafe fn`). Invocation is by `CRYPTO_free_ex_data` (public `unsafe extern "C"`) from `OwnedEngine::Drop`.
dynamic_data_ctx_free_func.q1_safe_caller_ub: No. A safe Rust caller cannot name or call a private `unsafe extern "C"` fn; the only in-crate path is an unsafe fn / unsafe block, and the registration path is unsafe.
dynamic_data_ctx_free_func.q2_unsafe_ops_covered: Yes. `OwnedCtx::<DynamicDataCtx>::from_raw_at` (which returns None for NULL/misaligned) is the single release; the index is created with this hook (eng_dyn.rs:499) and the only writer of the index stores `*mut DynamicDataCtx` (dynamic_set_data_ctx, eng_dyn.rs:467).
dynamic_data_ctx_free_func.q3_hidden_obligation: None found. A repeated CRYPTO_free_ex_data on the same block is safe: the body zeroes the slot and OPENSSL_sk after the callbacks (runtime/ex_data.rs:514-525), so a second invocation passes NULL to the hook and from_raw_at answers None. The doc's cited lines have drifted (:481-488 -> :499-504, :453 -> :467) but the establishing witnesses are present.
dynamic_data_ctx_free_func.q4_load_bearing_control: Yes in principle: B56-C7 counts exactly one release of the context block on the real ENGINE path and mutation M5 (a second CRYPTO_free) makes it fail; not re-run here (no build). Source-level C7 confirms the hook is never called outside an unsafe context.
dynamic_data_ctx_free_func.discharge: Contract at the definition + construction witnesses + ex_data free-hook contract (runtime/ex_data.rs:503-513) + control C7 (PASS baseline).

engine_list_cleanup.q1_safe_caller_ub: No. A safe caller cannot reach it; the test caller holds the lock precondition explicitly.
engine_list_cleanup.q2_unsafe_ops_covered: Yes. The body takes the lock before reading the head (the deliberate fix for the authority's TOCTOU) and removes it with the unlocked `engine_list_remove`; a panic unwinds to the `extern "C"` boundary and aborts, leaving no poisoned lock in a live process.

external_serialisation_adjudication.question: Is the retained second-concurrent-free / release-race obligation a real precondition on a safe caller, or a documented C-ABI obligation?
external_serialisation_adjudication.answer: It is a documented C-ABI (unsafe-caller) obligation, not a safe-caller obligation. SSL_CONF_CTX_free and every SSL_CONF entry point are `pub unsafe extern "C" fn`, so no safe Rust caller can invoke them. The requirement is stated verbatim in the function's # Safety ('The caller must externally serialise this call'), and it is the same object-lifetime rule the authority imposes: an OpenSSL object must not be freed or entered while another thread is inside it, and the C objects are not internally synchronised. Under §7 criterion 2 an external ABI contract can discharge a precondition, so the residual is classified as a retained external ABI contract, not an unestablished code precondition.
external_serialisation_adjudication.is_it_hidden: No. It is recorded in the receipt and stated at the interface. The b78 argument calls it a hidden obligation; this review disagrees with that label while agreeing that it is retained, not discharged by code.
external_serialisation_adjudication.does_it_block_criterion3: No, by itself: criterion 3 quantifies over safe Rust callers, and there is none for this entry point. It does not rescue the mechanism, which fails on F-SSL-1/2/3.
external_serialisation_adjudication.caveat: The candidate defers the release rather than refusing it; that is a recorded divergence and must not be described as making concurrent use safe.

The measured safe-pub surface does not replace it: only 30/290 obligations are reachable from an external safe pub fn, and criterion 3 for the other 260 still requires that each unsafe entry point's contract be complete and that its callers establish it. The cheapest order is: (1) fix the five confirmed safe-interface defects (F-BIO-1, F-SSL-2, F-SSL-3 and the two contract-placement rejects) because they block every mechanism and are mechanical; (2) re-issue the stale receipts (v1l F09, B56 engine_list_cleanup, the sslconf row) at the frozen S; (3) review the 207 with the b78 cohort method in dependency clusters, prioritising the 30 reachable from safe pub fns (criterion 3 first) and the mechanisms with contract-form gaps (EVP 36 operation-level-only, X509 2 no-contract); (4) only then run a BOUNDARY gate with TSan/Loom for RUNTIME_CONCURRENCY and a re-adjudication by a reviewer who is not the orchestrator.
task3_remaining.why_not_a_source_only_argument: A safe-pub-surface argument can discharge criterion 3 (no safe caller can cause UB) but not criterion 1 (every unsafe op has an explicit validity contract) or criterion 2 (every precondition is established by its callers). The 260 unsafe-entry-only obligations are reached by C consumers, and their contracts are the ABI evidence that must be read. There is no sound shortcut that turns 207 unreviewed caller closures into a discharge.

findings.statement: COMP_get_type (src/runtime/bio/comp.rs:237) and COMP_get_name (:252) are safe `pub extern "C" fn`s that dereference a caller-supplied `*const CompMethod`; the only guard is a NULL check and the pointer's contract is a comment plus `#[allow(clippy::not_unsafe_ptr_arg_deref)]`. Safe Rust can call them with a dangling pointer and cause UB. This is a criterion-3 counterexample inside the BIO mechanism directory and is not recorded in evidence/b78-safety-argument.json.
findings.control: source read; the pattern is the one the allow attribute documents

findings.statement: update_cipher_list_by_id and set_ciphersuites require exclusive access to the cipher-list slot and free the previous stack, but SSL_CTX_set_cipher_list, SSL_set_cipher_list, SSL_CTX_set_ciphersuites and SSL_set_ciphersuites state only 'NULL or live; NULL or NUL-terminated'. A concurrent reader (e.g. SSL_CTX_get_ciphers) is not excluded by the stated contract.
findings.control: C6 FAIL baseline; M6 PASS (statement added)

findings.statement: ssl_set_version_bound (src/ssl/ssl_conf.rs:567) is a safe `pub(crate) fn` with a raw `*mut c_int` parameter and an unchecked `unsafe { *bound = version }`. Any in-crate safe caller can pass a dangling pointer and cause UB (AGENTS.md §1: a safe fn that can trigger UB is a soundness bug even when today's call sites are correct).
findings.control: source read; mech-surface.json lists it as the only plain-Rust-ABI safe fn with a raw pointer parameter in the three mechanisms

findings.statement: SSL_COMP_get_name (src/ssl/ssl_ciph.rs:1800) is a safe `pub extern "C" fn` whose # Notes (not # Safety) require `comp` to be a live COMP_METHOD; it forwards to COMP_get_name, which dereferences it.

B56's engine_list_cleanup row describes a body that no longer exists: the lock-first rewrite (0d39697ae, 180 insertions) is not an ancestor of the B56 candidate, and the row's argument ('With a NULL lock the loop's ENGINE_remove answers 0') does not describe the current body. The span hash matches the current operation, so the closure accepts the obligation, but the receipt's reasoning is not evidence for it.
The v1l receipt bound to push_cstr_or_null REJECTS it (F09, no # Safety) while the current source has the contract. The closure records DISCHARGED on a rejected receipt.
findings.control: C1 PASS on push_cstr_or_null; M4 reproduces F09 when the # Safety is removed

findings.statement: The b78 argument's safe-surface numbers ('13 safe pub fn in mechanism files', 'crate-wide safe pub fn count is 202') have no recorded tool and do not match the measurement (879 safe pub definitions; 477 reaching unsafe).

non_claims: No build, test, Miri, ASan, TSan or Loom run supports this review; all controls are source-level.
The name-based call graph is not a rustc-level resolution; dynamic dispatch, trait objects and macro-expanded edges are under-approximated, and re-exports were not followed.
This review does not re-adjudicate the 207 obligations outside the four remaining mechanisms' b78 cohort, nor any obligation outside the 21.

The safe-pointer functions listed are the ones verified by reading the body; the count of 46 raw-pointer safe extern C functions is a lexical over-approximation that includes the 33 pointer-ignoring QUIC stubs.
Accepting the SSL_CONF_CTX_free serialisation as an external ABI contract is a classification of the obligation, not evidence that any C consumer observes it.
